notes: A silent mortal is pulled into the void on the ninth MUD hour (timer > IDLE_TO_VOID 8, one check per point_update). Restored with DP-1311: IDLE_TO_VOID is 8 again, commands reset the timer before dispatch (comm.c:600-601), the wall-clock reaper is gone, and the frozen-clock heartbeat now carries point_update (cmd/server/main.go OnPointUpdate behind dpclock.Frozen).

Any command from a voided player returns them to their room with "$n has returned." to that room's other occupants only (act TO_ROOM excludes the actor); the scenario's look proves C's return byte for byte (R1).

At sunset C loads the moon-matched blue portal and opens one ghost-ship dock/ship exit pair; sunrise removes them. Each send_to_room message reaches only awake players in its source room. DP-1316 (R1/R3/R4).

Eight MUD hours of silence stay on the near side of the threshold: check_idling compares timer > IDLE_TO_VOID (8), so the void lands on the ninth point_update and not the eighth. The immortal peer's own look at the eighth hour still lists the actor in the room and no departure act has appeared (R1/R3).

The voided player's departure is act("$n disappears into the void.", TO_ROOM) in the room they are leaving, emitted before the move to Limbo (char_to_room(ch, 1)). The same-room immortal peer receives exactly that line; the actor receives only its own "pulled into a void" line. DP-1311 put the port's room line back on game.Act so the transfer can no longer swallow it (R1/R4).

A command dequeued for a voided character returns them to GET_WAS_IN before dispatch and emits act("$n has returned.", TO_ROOM) in that room (comm.c:607). The peer sees exactly that line; the returnee never receives its own return message (R1/R2).

Per-recipient bytes for the whole void round trip: the actor sees only "You have been idle, and are pulled into a void." on the ninth tick, and the room peer sees only "$n disappears into the void." and later "$n has returned."; neither audience receives the other's line (R1).

An accepted command line resets char_specials.timer at the game-loop dequeue point, before dispatch, so eight further silent hours leave the player in the room and the void arrives on the ninth hour after the command, not the ninth hour of the session. The ~dpclock control line is consumed before C's input queue (comm.c:2027) and therefore must not reset the timer. DP-1311 restored the reset at the seam both transports share (R1/R2).

C moves the still-connected idler with char_to_room(ch, 3), whose room argument is an RNUM: with the shipped zone order rnum 3 is vnum 4 ("Frontline's Sphere"), so close_socket's act("$n has lost $s link.") reaches vnum 4's occupants. The port's PlayerTransfer(p, 3) resolves a VNUM, so its act reaches vnum 3 ("A Totally Empty Room"). A peer placed in each room exposes it both ways: C's vnum-4 peer sees the act and the port's does not, and the port's vnum-3 peer sees it while C's does not. Blocked pending the destination fix; see handoff/2026-09-27-idle-lifecycle-expansion.md (R1/R5e).

The connected branch calls close_socket inside check_idling and NULLs ch->desc, so C never returns the character to the menu. The transport close itself is comparable with the harness `compare-close` marker and the spike matched <CLOSE> on both engines, but the same probe block also carries a byte only the port emits: at the disconnect pulse C queues that hour's outdoor weather line and close_socket then discards it (comm.c:2092 runs before the game loop's output pass, comm.c:636), while the port flushes it to the socket before retiring the session. Blocked pending that ordering fix; see handoff/2026-09-27-idle-lifecycle-expansion.md (R1).

Because C frees the descriptor before extract_char, extract_char_final's "hand the connection back to the menu" arm never runs for an idle force-rent. The spike's actor block contained no menu bytes on either engine, but the claim cannot be promoted while the same block still differs on the weather byte above; see handoff/2026-09-27-idle-lifecycle-expansion.md (R1/R4).

C keeps a force-rented character's rentable objects in the rent file (free_rent is YES, config.c:106) and restores them through Crash_load on the next menu entry, while unrentable objects are destroyed. The vehicle that would compare the port's inventory bytes after <RELOGIN> runs through the same force-rent branch, so it is blocked by the disconnect-pulse byte above; see handoff/2026-09-27-idle-lifecycle-expansion.md (R1).

An equipped NORENT object is unequipped to the character by Crash_extract_norents_from_equipped and then destroyed by Crash_extract_norents, so it must not come back on re-entry: the leak DP-1311 fixed. The oracle vehicle that would prove it (disposable spawned NORENT inventory and equipped objects, forced through the idle force-rent, then compared after <RELOGIN>) is blocked by the same disconnect-pulse byte; the state claim is held by pkg/session/reaper_test.go until then (R1/R5f).

The reset counter is proven by behavior, not by state inspection: the immortal peer's look at the eighth hour after the command still lists the actor in the original room, and one more hour voids them. A port that ignores the reset voids inside that window; a port that resets on harness clock control never voids at all (R1/R3).
